title: How To Create Knitwear In Clo! Skill-Up Webinar
description:
Follow along with the files here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/12lPgUklm4mFDd7rTijGpNOgWEqS2q9dY

This Skill-up Webinar focuses on the realistic knitwear settings in CLO. We covered the current options for knitwear, applying patches on top of the knitwear, making a "fur cable", creating felt tree patches, and adding mini Christmas lights on top of the knitwear.

This live session took place in December 2024. Join our next webinar to participate and ask questions live!

Chapters:
00:00 Finished project overview
04:26 - Knitwear settings
34:57 - Adding the dog patch
42:55 - Adjusting the felt tree patch material
49:15 - Creating the fur cable topstitch
57:10 - Creating light-up bulbs
1:06:00 - Q&A

Questions? Comment below or ask in our CLO discord server: https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/7814962429977-How-can-I-join-CLO-Discord- 

--- 
Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/itsclo3d 
LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/company/clo-virtual-fashion-inc-/ 
Facebook: https://www.facebook.com/clo3d/

summary: ```markdown # How To Create Knitwear In Clo! Skill-Up Webinar ## Introduction Welcome to today's Skill-Up Webinar, where we will explore how to create beautiful knitwear in Clo. We will focus on a stunning knitwear outfit featuring a skirt and a beret, designed by Celia from the Spanish team. Our primary focus will be on the knitwear aspects, including the patches and lighting effects. ## Setting Up the Scene Before we begin, I need to turn on the render. Some elements we're creating are only visible in the render, such as lights, fur, and patch displacement. The new realistic knitwear function can be resource-intensive, so please be patient as it loads. ### Opening the Project - Open the file named **scale up knitwear start**. - Close the library by pressing the letter **Y** on your keyboard. ## Understanding the Knitwear Function The knitwear texture or function was introduced in the **Clo 2024 version**. If you're using an older version, you may not have access to this feature. ### Material Setup - Our outfit currently lacks detail, so we will focus on materials and patches. - Some patches, like the trees, are already applied, and we will be adding lights later. ## Working on Knitwear Material ### Changing Material Type 1. Select the **2x2 rib** material in the property editor. 2. Navigate to the material section to select from multiple material types, such as shiny fabric or fur. 3. Choose the **knitwear** option, which may take some time to load. ### Understanding 3D Mesh Structure Each loop of the knitwear becomes its own 3D mesh structure, resulting in realistic textures but also heavier computational requirements. ### Stitching Types We have several stitching presets available. Currently, we will use: - **Garter**, - **Stockinette**, - **Reverse Stitch**, - **Seed**, - **Moss**, - **1x1 Rib**, - **2x2 Rib** (our selection), - **Honeycomb**. ### Yarn Thickness and Gauge - The yarn thickness is adjustable. For example, setting it to **2** gives a standard thickness, while increasing it to **5** results in a thicker yarn. - The gauge is calculated per inch and affects the tightness of the loops. Ranging from **1 to 16**, higher settings can slow down your computer. ### Knit Direction You can adjust the knit direction for specific designs, such as raglan sleeves. The default is **0 degrees**. ### Apply Amount & Ply Color - The number of yarns can range from **1 ply** to **6 ply**. - Choose colors from the color tab; for instance, use darker shades for a richer look. ### Randomization Enable randomization to create irregularities in color patterns, adding realism to your knitwear. ### Yarn Variance Adjust the yarn variance for texture irregularities to make the knitwear appear more handmade. ## Adding Patches ### Importing Graphics - Navigate to the **training folder** and find the **happy holidays box patch**. - Drag and drop the main texture into the graphic tab of the object browser. ### Adjusting the Z-Offset To ensure the patch appears on top of the knitwear, adjust the **Z offset** to **1.7** or more, depending on yarn thickness. ## Applying Additional Fabrics For the tree patches, apply the necessary maps from the **boucle fabric** folder to enhance realism. ## Creating Decorative Elements ### Top Stitch for Light Cables 1. Create a new top stitch called **cable light**. 2. Adjust the offset to align it with the knitwear. 3. Select **fur** as the material type and choose a color that complements the design. ### Adding Light Trims 1. Switch to the **trim tab** and locate the **light trim**. 2. Drag and drop it onto the patches in the scene. 3. Ensure the material type is set to **light** for emitting effects. ## Finalizing the Render Now, we can preview the render. If everything is set correctly, our lights should shine, enhancing the overall design. ## Conclusion Thank you for joining this Skill-Up Webinar! I hope you learned valuable techniques for creating realistic knitwear in Clo. If you have any questions, feel free to ask. Happy knitting and see you in the next webinar! ```
